name: SNB Capital
legal_name: SNB Capital Company (a Saudi Closed Joint Stock Company; website footer says 'Saudi Joint Stock Company'); formerly NCB Capital Company
founded: Per audited FS note 1: formed under CMA Resolution 2-83-2005 (28 Jun 2005 as printed) and registered under CR 1010231474 dated 17 Apr 2007; AR 2025: licensed activities began 25 Jun 2007; CMA licence 37-06046. Operating firm since the 2021 NCB-Samba merger (NCB Capital merged with Samba Capital).
ownership_summary: 100% owned by Saudi National Bank (150,000,000 shares of SAR 10; unchanged from 2024). Paid-up capital SAR 1,500,000,000 (FS note 14; website footer). Also has SAR 1bn Tier 1 Sukuk (issued 2023) in equity.
government_link: Indirect. The parent, Saudi National Bank, is 37.2% owned by the Public Investment Fund (see sa-snb).
group_structure: 100% subsidiary of Saudi National Bank (sa-snb). SNB reports SNB Capital as its 'Capital Market' segment (wealth, asset management, investment banking, brokerage). Double counting: SNB Capital's balance sheet, income and AUM are inside SNB group figures; never add this record to sa-snb. The segment figures differ from SNB Capital's standalone statements (FY2025 segment operating income SAR 2,422m vs standalone SAR 4,122m) because of inter-segment and treasury items. Business divisions (website): Asset Management, Wealth Management, Securities, Investment Banking, SNB Capital (DIFC), Principal Investments and Funding.

footprint: Head office: SNB Regional Building, King Saud Road, Riyadh. Nationwide presence in Saudi Arabia; VIP trading lounges 'across the Kingdom'; branch count not published. International: SNB Capital (DIFC) Limited, Dubai (DFSA), plus Cayman and UAE vehicles. International brokerage covers about 30 markets (checked 12 Oct 2026).
customer_segments: Individual investors (retail via AlAhli Tadawul and the SNB Capital app; SNB account holders via Idikhari; individual and institutional wealth clients via Wealth Managers' Coverage); public- and private-sector employers (Idikhari, employee share plans, corporate savings); government and endowments (Namaa Endowment Fund, waqf funds); corporates and governments (investment banking, DCM/ECM); foreign institutions (market access, custody).
business_lines: Asset management (public funds, DPM, private funds, REITs, alternatives); Wealth management (investment advisory, Wealth Managers' Coverage, Idikhari and corporate savings); Securities (local and international brokerage, margin financing, securities lending, custody and securities services, employee share plans, market access); Investment banking (ECM, DCM, M&A, debt and corporate finance advisory); Principal investments and funding (largest exposure fixed income; Moody's A2 standalone, AA+ Tassnief); SNB Capital (DIFC) private funds. FY2025 fees (SAR '000): asset management 982,308; securities 272,764; investment banking 139,387; total fees 1,394,459 of total operating income 4,122,069 (the rest is investment and margin income).

capabilities.wealth_summary: SNB Capital is the 100% capital-markets subsidiary of Saudi National Bank, CMA-licensed (37-06046) for dealing, underwriting, managing, arranging, advising and custody, with a DFSA-regulated sister entity in DIFC. It reports AUM of SAR 263.0bn at end-2025 (asset management division; 'largest in the market') and SAR 279bn at 1Q 2026 (22% share, #1). FY2025 net profit was SAR 2,518m on total operating income of SAR 4,122m; asset management fees were SAR 982m and securities fees SAR 273m (down 40%). The fund shelf is its own, mostly Shariah-compliant: 21 equity funds (incl. four MSCI Islamic index funds), about 12 liquidity and fixed-income funds, 11 multi-asset and waqf funds, REITs, real estate and DIFC private funds. Retail execution runs through AlAhli Tadawul and the SNB Capital app (Saudi plus about 30 international markets via Interactive Brokers and a second 'GTN' schedule), and the Idikhari plan gives SNB account holders goal-based, automated fund savings from SAR 100. The group says a robo-advisory platform is being added to Wealth Management, and its 2025-27 strategy includes 'establish partnerships to expand and deepen client offerings'. Wealth leadership changed in March 2026: Mohammed Al-Saggaf moved from Head of Wealth Management to Head of Client Relations and Distribution, and the website now lists no Head of Wealth Management or Head of Asset Management.

private_banking.detail: Private banking sits in the parent bank (SNB Private Banking; see sa-snb). SNB Capital offers 'Wealth Managers' Coverage' for individual and institutional clients: a dedicated team of professional wealth managers, bespoke strategies, financial planning and access to alternatives (private equity, real estate, hedge funds). No eligibility threshold is published.

asset_management.detail: SAR 263.0bn AUM at end-2025; 22% KSA share and #1 at 1Q 2026 (SAR 279bn). Website categories: liquidity and fixed income, public equity, multi-asset, alternative, private funds and REITs. 2025: 18 new products per SNB's annual report (20 new funds per SNB Capital's own report), including 13 private real estate funds, a waqf fund and three international credit funds. Per its own report: Moody's MQ1 (highest) investment-quality rating and a 2025 'best multi-asset manager' award from Forbes Middle East. Namaa Endowment Fund (Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture) appointed SNB Capital as manager in Feb 2026.

brokerage.detail: Saudi Exchange: #1 broker, 14% of H1 2026 value traded (SAR 175bn); more than 15% in 2025; over 25% of retail IPO subscriptions. Channels: AlAhli Tadawul online, mobile app and IVR, VIP trading lounges across the Kingdom, free live prices, Mubasher Net and Mubasher Pro. International: '30 markets' per the website (US, UK, UAE, Kuwait, Egypt, Oman, Bahrain and several European and Asian markets in the price list), with Interactive Brokers named as execution partner (IBKR Pro, IBKR Lite, US options) and a separate 'GTN' schedule for Asia-Pacific, US and GCC/Arab markets; nearly USD 8bn traded in 2025 (+44%). Margin financing (+about 40% in 2025), securities lending, employee share plans, custody (AUC SAR 155bn) and a market-access service for foreign institutions (over 150,000 end-client accounts opened).

digital_investing.detail: 'SNB Capital' app (iOS, seller The Saudi National Bank; v2.20.19, updated 11 Sep 2026; first released 24 Dec 2020; 2,116 ratings, average 2.81): trading, dashboard, order placing, cash transfers to and from portfolios. AlAhli Tadawul online platform and mobile app for Saudi and international markets; Idikhari goal-based savings is enrolled inside the SNB Capital app. Fund subscriptions in-app were not confirmed by the listing. Chief Digital Officer role exists (Loai Bafaqeeh).

advisory.detail: CMA licence includes advising; Wealth Management is a standalone division. Investment Advisory page: personalised portfolio management, financial planning and wealth structuring, market insights; Wealth Managers' Coverage team. No named advisory platform, thresholds or adviser profiles published. A LinkedIn search snippet suggested a 'Head of Investment Advisory and Solutions' role from May 2026; not verified, not recorded as a person.

discretionary.detail: Discretionary Portfolio Management (DPM) listed under Asset Management ('expert-led strategies aligned with investors' goals and risk profiles across all asset classes'); assets held in a fiduciary capacity for the parent bank were SAR 1.76bn at end-2025 (note 21). No DPM minimum published.

model_portfolios_robo.detail: Idikhari (individual savings plan) in the SNB Capital app: goal-based plans (vehicle, education, wedding, property, travel, savings, retirement) that assess goal, savings and risk appetite, recommend one Shariah-compliant fund per plan (SNB Capital SAR Multi-Asset Conservative, Moderate or Growth funds, or Al Sunbullah SAR) and automate standing-order contributions from SAR 100. This is single-fund recommendation, not multi-asset model portfolios. SNB's AR 2025 says a robo-advisory platform 'is being added to the portfolio of Wealth Management services'; no launch found. Feb 2024 MoU with fintech Mala'a (digital financial planning, automated investing).

funds_platform.detail: SNB Capital distributes its own funds (app, AlAhli Tadawul, SNB branches). No third-party fund shelf or fund-platform provider found. Feb 2026 Investcorp partnership covers asset management, investment banking and wealth management for alternatives (private equity, real assets, credit), scope of distribution not specified.

structured_products.detail: No structured products on the SNB Capital website pages opened. SNB Capital won a 'Best in Saudi Arabia' award for Islamic Structured Finance in July 2026 (corporate finance, per media list). The parent bank lists structured products for private-banking clients (see sa-snb).

private_markets.detail: Alternatives are a core line: real estate funds (e.g. SEDCO Residential Development Fund, SNB Capital Real Estate Fund, AlAhli REIT Fund (1)), private equity and venture, 13 private real estate funds launched in 2025. SNB Capital (DIFC) Limited (DFSA-regulated, over SAR 7.5bn AUM, undated) manages 14 named funds: aviation (I, II), credit (I, II, IV), real estate credit (I, II), asset-backed income, GP stakes, Pan-European real estate, oil and gas, strategic equity, private equity solutions, software opportunities. Parent group also holds SNB Capital Dubai Inc. (private equity and real estate in emerging markets). Wealth Managers' Coverage offers access to private equity, real estate and hedge funds. Investcorp partnership (Feb 2026) for private equity, real assets, credit; Orion partnership (Jan 2026) for mining.

islamic_wealth.detail: SNB Capital's AR says its products and services are Shariah-compliant and that it is the largest Shariah-compliant asset manager in the world; all public funds on the website state Shariah compliance or track MSCI Islamic M-Series indices (equity, sukuk, murabaha/money market, waqf funds, Sadaqqat charity fund). Whole-firm Shariah-only status is not stated in the audited statements, which include Tier 1 Sukuk, bank borrowings and margin lending, so 'model' is left as Not applicable.

partners.what: Global Trading page lists IBKR Pro, IBKR Lite and US Options IBKR commission schedules; IBKR is named as execution partner (products on the page: equities, options and ETFs; US bonds are also priced). Pricing is also listed for France, Portugal, Germany, Belgium, Switzerland, Singapore and Poland without naming the broker per market

partners.what: A second commission schedule ('For all commission related to GTN') covers Australia, China, Hong Kong, Indonesia, Japan, Malaysia, Philippines, Singapore, Thailand and US plus GCC/Arab markets (Egypt, Muscat, Kuwait, Bahrain, UAE, Nasdaq Dubai). The provider's identity is not stated on the page; relationship type inferred from the commission-sheet label only

Idikhari requires an SNB current account (standing orders); SNB Capital earns management and performance fees on funds and manages SNB assets (note 21); parent forms Group collaboration lever in strategy

MoU for SNB Capital clients to access Mala'a's digital financial planning and wealth management (robo-advisory) services and for Mala'a clients to access SNB Capital funds; announced at SNB Capital's Investment Tycoons Forum

initiatives.what: SNB Capital Batteries Fund (Shariah-compliant, ESG-themed, invests in SK On) and 2024 Ahalina and Financial Awareness programmes listed on the strategic initiatives page; 15 Jun 2023 board placed all management committees under the CEO. Awards page lists 2024 Saudi Capital Market Awards (Investment Bank of the Year, Most Active Derivatives Broker) and 2024 Euromoney Islamic Finance awards; no 2025-26 awards listed there

Asset management launched 18 new products (SNB annual report) / 20 new funds (SNB Capital annual report), incl. 13 private real estate funds, a waqf fund and three international credit funds; diversified into alternatives, money markets and fixed income and multi-asset funds

Investment banking closed its 100th transaction since the 2021 merger (total value above SAR 750bn); more than 25 deals in 2025 incl. the SAR 7.13bn ACWA Power rights issue; over 50% share in ECM and 70% in DCM
SNB's annual report: Asset Management is a core contributor to a robo-advisory platform being added to Wealth Management services; asset management business areas encouraged to deploy AI

Idikhari employee savings programme reached about SAR 24bn AUM and about 90,000 participants; 2025-27 strategy levers: market-leading position, digital client experience, SNB Group collaboration, partnerships to expand client offerings
Strategic partnership with Orion Resource Partners to support the Kingdom's mining and midstream projects
Strategic partnership with Investcorp Saudi Arabia for alternatives (private equity, real assets, credit) across asset management, investment banking and wealth management
Appointed fund manager of the Namaa Endowment Fund launched by the Ministry of Environment, Water and Agriculture (Shariah-compliant public offering)

Leadership reshuffle: Mohammed Al-Saggaf became Head of Client Relations and Distribution (from Head of Wealth Management); Naif Al-Saif became Chief Investment Officer; Mohammed Al Ali became Head of Real Estate Investments
Financial close of a USD 456m ECA financing announced
Named 'Best in Saudi Arabia' for ECM, Research and Islamic Structured Finance

SNB 2Q 2026 deck: SNB Capital #1 in AUM and brokerage share, #3 in investment banking (2025 revenue basis); 2027 targets are #1 in all three. Capital Markets segment income before zakat fell 22% in H1 2026 on softer market volumes
Hosted 'Growth Connect' event bringing Saudi-listed companies and investors together
SNB Capital app v2.20.19 released (stability and performance enhancements)

opportunities: SNB's AR 2025 says a robo-advisory platform 'is being added to the portfolio of Wealth Management services'; no launch announced as of 12 Oct 2026 (S6)
Existing goal-based product (Idikhari) recommends one fund per plan from four funds, so it has no multi-asset model portfolios (S15)

Fees from securities fell 40% in FY2025 and 32% in H1 2026 while asset management fees held (SAR 982m, S4; H1 2026 SAR 417m vs 437m, S7), so recurring-fee wealth solutions are a stated priority ('SNB Capital fee focus' in the parent strategy)
Strategy lever 'establish partnerships to expand and deepen client offerings' (S6); recent partners are alternatives managers (Investcorp, Feb 2026) and a fintech MoU (Mala'a, Feb 2024)
Wealth leadership in transition: Head of Wealth Management became Head of Client Relations and Distribution in March 2026 and no Head of Wealth or Asset Management is listed on the website (S1, S2)
iOS app rating 2.81 on 2,116 ratings (S31) against a stated goal of enhancing client experience with digital platforms (S6)
barriers: Scale and in-house manufacturing: SAR 263bn AUM, #1 in KSA, with its own funds across equity, fixed income, multi-asset and alternatives, and 96% of AUM in the top two performance quartiles per the parent AR (S4, S6)
Group captive distribution through SNB and an existing global execution stack (Interactive Brokers, GTN) (S12, S13)
Shariah-compliant product expectations: nearly all funds are Shariah-compliant (S5, S20, S21)
Existing partnerships with alternatives managers (Investcorp, Orion) reduce need for third-party private-markets shelf (S26, S27)

discrepancies.field: Operating income, net income, total assets: standalone vs parent segment
discrepancies.detail: SNB Capital's audited FS show FY2025 total operating income SAR 4,122,069k, net income before zakat SAR 2,697,869k and total assets SAR 32,958,184k. SNB's annual report shows the Capital Markets segment at operating income SAR 2,422m, net income before zakat SAR 1,731m and total assets SAR 33,634m. SNB Capital's own annual report quotes net income before zakat of SAR 2.69bn (standalone).
discrepancies.resolution: Used the standalone audited FS as the primary figures; recorded the parent segment figures as separate 'parent_segment_*' proxies. The gap (investment and treasury income, inter-segment items) was not reconciled in the sources.

discrepancies.detail: SNB annual report says Asset Management launched 18 new products; SNB Capital's annual report says it launched more than twenty products and its key-figures page says 20 new funds.
discrepancies.resolution: Both recorded in the initiatives line. Unresolved; likely differing scope (funds vs products).

discrepancies.detail: SNB Capital's key-figures page shows SAR 155bn assets under custody; SNB's annual report says AUC reached SAR 156bn.
discrepancies.resolution: Used SNB Capital's own figure (155bn) and noted the other. Minor.

discrepancies.detail: SNB Capital's annual report gives 23%+ market share of AUM (end-2025); SNB's 2Q26 deck gives 22% at 1Q 2026 (SAR 279bn of SAR 1,286bn).

AR 2025 lists Mohammed Al-Saggaf as head of wealth, Naif Al-Saif as head of private investments and funding, Loai Bafaqeeh as head of securities and acting IT head, Khalid Al-Bairakan as head of asset management and Abdulrahman Almashal as 'Chief Administrator'. The website (12 Oct 2026) shows March 2026 appointments (Al-Saggaf, Al-Saif, Al Ali), Jalal Faruki as Head of Securities, Bafaqeeh as Chief Digital Officer, Alghursan as Acting Chief of Staff, and no head of asset management or wealth management.
discrepancies.resolution: Used the website for the current roster. Al-Bairakan and Almashal recorded as 'Requires verification'.

discrepancies.detail: The wealth management page describes Idikhari as a corporate savings initiative for employees; the Idikhari page describes an individual goal-based savings plan; the AR counts about 90,000 employees in the programme.
discrepancies.resolution: Treated as one programme with corporate and individual channels. Minor.

open_items: No 30 Jun 2026 standalone statements or AUM: SNB Capital publishes annual statements only. Balance sheet and income are FY2025; H1 2026 data comes from the parent's segment note and presentation (proxies) and AUM is 1Q 2026.

Head of Asset Management and Head of Wealth Management not identified: the AR 2025 lists Khalid Al-Bairakan (asset management) and Mohammed Al-Saggaf (wealth) but the website no longer lists either role. Check for a March 2026 reorganisation announcement (Saudi Exchange issuer announcements returned no result in search; not fetched, 403 risk).

LinkedIn checks for CEO, wealth, securities, digital and investments heads returned no matching profiles; all marked 'Not verified'. Unrelated LinkedIn results in the same searches (a 'Head of Investment Advisory and Solutions' appointed May 2026; two other profiles describing wealth and multi-asset leadership roles) were not matched to an official source and are not recorded.

'GTN' vendor identity not stated on the site (only a commission schedule label); the Android package ID 'it.elfisystems.gbs.ncbc.phone' and iOS bundle ID 'com.alahlitadawul.gbs.mobile' suggest a third-party brokerage app vendor but no source confirms it. An undated trade-news item (seen in search results only) reports NCB Capital implementing Fidessa; current stack unconfirmed.
The robo-advisory platform mentioned in SNB's AR 2025 had no launch announcement found; scope (client-facing vs adviser tool) unknown.
Total client numbers, app users and employee headcount not disclosed. SNB Capital (DIFC) AUM (over SAR 7.5bn) is undated; DFSA licence number and register entry not checked.
CMA authorised-persons register entry not checked directly (licence 37-06046 taken from the firm's own site and FS); Saudi Exchange pages not used.

SNB Capital's Arabic annual report has a garbled text layer; figures were read from page renders (PDF p.5, 6, 8, 18). Pages on organisational structure, awards and product listings were summarised by the fetch tool, so exact fund counts are 'as listed on the website' and may omit funds shown only in PDFs. One fetched page (organizational chart) returned a note that its text contained a hidden formatting-instruction section; it was ignored.

Parent file sa-snb says 'Mala'a MoU' and 'BNY Mellon' relate to SNB Capital: confirmed here as a Feb 2024 MoU (status unknown now) and a Dec 2021 headline respectively; the parent's 'IBKR, GTN' leads are confirmed only as commission-schedule labels.
